title: Telemetry dispatch heartbeat
description: contract_revision: 1 (new schema — dispatch-liveness convention). A liveness pulse a running dispatch may emit between long steps, referencing an in-flight dispatch_id (see telemetry-dispatch-record.json). Deliberately a SIBLING record, not an added telemetry-dispatch-record.json status value: the dispatch-record schema is a strict pre-spawn/terminal state machine (one in_flight write, one terminal write) and a heartbeat is neither — it is non-terminal, may be emitted any number of times, and carries no completed_ts/result_summary. Keeping it a separate schema leaves telemetry-dispatch-record.json's existing shape and DISPATCH_STATUSES enum completely unchanged (true backward compatibility, not just additive-enum), and lets heartbeat-specific fields (progress) evolve independently. A consumer correlates heartbeats to a dispatch by dispatch_id and treats the most recent heartbeat ts (relative to now) as its liveness signal, distinguishing still-working from stalled without polling unrelated proxies (git HEAD, output-file mtime). loadout defines the record shape and a sink-routed emitter only — it does not decide heartbeat cadence, does not schedule emission, and does not itself detect staleness; that consumption logic is a deployment/harness concern (CLAUDE.md hard rule 2). additionalProperties:false, mechanical whitelist.

dispatch_id.description: The dispatch this heartbeat belongs to — matches the dispatch_id of the telemetry-dispatch-record.json in_flight write for the same dispatch. Shape is caller-defined, same convention as the dispatch-record schema.

ts.description: ISO 8601 UTC timestamp when this heartbeat was emitted.

progress.description: Optional short, non-prose step/progress label (e.g. "running test suite", "tool round 4"). Purely descriptive — no schema-enforced vocabulary, a consumer treats it as opaque display text.
